evals.prompt: A user reports: 'The main menu doesn't work with my screen reader, it's really frustrating.' No URL, no browser/AT version, no steps. How should this be handled?

required_concepts.label: preserves the report as a valid finding
requests task/behavior/reproduction context
any_of: what were you trying to do

prohibited_concepts.label: requires a diagnosis or disability disclosure
requires HTML/technical evidence from the reporter before accepting

evals.prompt: An axe-core scan flagged 'button-name' on https://example.gov/checkout. Describe what's needed before this becomes an actionable, remediation-ready finding.

prohibited_concepts.label: requires WCAG mapping or severity as a gate

evals.prompt: A reporter pastes this URL in a bug report: https://example.com/orders/847291?token=secret-value&email=jane@example.com. What should happen to the location field?

required_concepts.label: redacts the token and personal data

evals.prompt: The reported HTML source for a page shows a properly labeled button, but the automated scan still failed on it. What's the likely explanation and what evidence should be collected?

required_concepts.label: recognizes source HTML may not match runtime DOM

evals.prompt: A finding was reproduced last week. This week's comparable rerun, on the same resource and rule with successful page load and auth, found nothing. What lifecycle status applies, and what happens to the finding?
A scheduled rerun of a rule against a resource timed out before the page finished loading. What lifecycle status applies?

prohibited_concepts.label: treats it as absent or resolved

evals.prompt: A color-contrast finding on a dynamically generated marketing page reproduced twice out of five scan runs this month, but not the other three. How should this be tracked?

required_concepts.label: records a review or expiry date

prohibited_concepts.label: keeps it with no owner or plan indefinitely
any_of: leave it open indefinitely with no plan

evals.prompt: A user with a documented history of using a screen reader reports that the checkout submit button is unreachable by keyboard on a payment page. Internal QA could not reproduce it in one attempt. How should this be handled given the task is payment-related?

required_concepts.label: does not reject based on failed internal reproduction alone
any_of: not proof the reporter was wrong

required_concepts.label: creates bounded investigation proportionate to consequence

prohibited_concepts.label: treats failed rerun as proof finding is invalid

evals.prompt: The same rule fails on 40 pages of a site. Should the task-level severity be escalated because of how many pages are affected?

required_concepts.label: keeps severity based on task impact
treats frequency/reach as a priority signal

prohibited_concepts.label: escalates severity purely from occurrence count
any_of: increase severity due to the number of pages

evals.prompt: A GitHub issue was filed to request a fresh accessibility scan of a site. The scan found 12 findings. Is the scan request issue the tracker ID for all 12?

required_concepts.label: distinguishes scan request from tracker ID

prohibited_concepts.label: treats scan request as the tracker for every finding
any_of: scan request is the tracker id for each
use the scan issue as the tracker for all

evals.prompt: Two findings from different pages have the same pattern fingerprint. Does this prove they share the same root cause?

required_concepts.label: requires investigation to confirm root cause

prohibited_concepts.label: treats matching fingerprint as proof of shared cause
any_of: proves they share the same root cause

evals.prompt: A developer merged a fix and the automated rule now passes. Is the issue ready to close?

prohibited_concepts.label: treats automated pass alone as sufficient to close
any_of: automated pass is enough to close
close it now that the rule passes

evals.prompt: A team wants to change how the pattern fingerprint is computed to fix a normalization bug. What has to happen to the existing a11y/pattern/v1 profile and its identifiers?

required_concepts.label: preserves the old profile and legacy identifiers

prohibited_concepts.label: edits the frozen profile in place

evals.prompt: A tester manually found a barrier with no automated tool involved and no way to compute a fingerprint for it. Is this a valid, acceptable finding?

required_concepts.label: accepts the manual finding without a fingerprint

prohibited_concepts.label: requires calculating or inventing a fingerprint
any_of: requires a fingerprint to be valid
